rules.rule: `port_id` is `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}`, unique per definition across all kinds.
The implicit IDs `in`, `then`, `failed`, `error`, `cancelled`, `body` and `completed` are reserved.
`event` ports are output-only.
Exec ports have no type.
`available_on` lists the exec outcome outs after which an `execution` output is defined; the default is `["then"]`.
The implicit `error: core/error@1` is available on `failed`.
A port `default` is not allowed for handle or stream types.
A `secret-ref` literal is only a reference, never secret material.
`optional` is allowed only if the type is `core/option@1<…>`.
`lazy` ports exist only on intrinsics in v1 (`select`, `and`, `or`, `coalesce`, `try`).
`group`, `label`, `description` and `editor` are presentation only and never semantic.
`sensitivity: sensitive` drives redaction in traces.
Action/async/iterator/control get `in` (unless the intrinsic names its inputs), `failed` and `error`; action/async/entry with no declared outcome outs get `then`; async and iterator get `cancelled`.
A definition with declared outcome outs replaces `then`.
Exactly one outcome out fires per execution; `failed` and `cancelled` are outcomes too.
A data out connects to a data in only if the types are identical after generic resolution.
A data out connected to an exec in is rejected.
An exec out connected to a data in is rejected.
An exec out connects to an exec in within the same region.
An event out connected to an exec in is OK and the target starts a new event region.
An event out connected to a data in is rejected.
A data input has at most one incoming edge.
A data output has unlimited edges (fan-out shares an immutable value).
A data output has at most one edge if its type is a stream.
An exec output has at most one edge.
An exec input accepts unlimited edges from the same region; merge is OR and each arriving token executes the node once.
An event output has at most one edge.
A data self edge is rejected unless §8 permits it.
An exec self edge is an ordinary control cycle (§8).
An input value resolves in order: connected edge, instance literal, definition default, `None` for an optional port, otherwise `E-INPUT-REQUIRED`.
When an edge is connected the instance literal stays in the document as shadowed and is ignored by the compiler; disconnecting restores it.
Literals exist only for types with a literal codec; handles, streams, results and errors have none.
Variadic instance ports use stable keys `item#k`, so inserting an item in the middle does not rewrite edges.
`k` is a per-node counter that is never reused.
Variadic order is the persisted instance order, not `k`.
Ports that depend on config or type arguments come from a declarative port template that the host evaluates; no guest code runs to compute ports.
Every non-intrinsic node persists a resolved signature snapshot; a missing package still shows ports and edges.
If re-resolution differs from the snapshot it produces a diagnostic.
Edges to vanished ports become orphan edges: preserved, displayed and not compiled.
Persisted documents and wire contracts use only the canonical type form; the editor short forms are display only.
A type parameter `$ident` appears only inside definitions.
A type lock records `named` without parameters, plus codec version.
`core/map@1<K,V>` is insertion-ordered.
A map key `K` must implement `hash` + `eq` and must not be a float.
`core/result@1<T>` is produced only by `core/try` and by nodes that explicitly return it.
`core/secret-ref@1` has no conversion to string and is never a literal secret.
i8/i16/u8/u16, decimals and tuples are excluded from v1, and there is no `any` type.
Types are nominal: two packages' `point` records are different types even with identical fields.
The major version is part of a type's identity.
`eq` is implemented by all core types except f32/f64, handles and streams.
`ord` on floats is available only through explicit `total-order` nodes.
Only the package that owns a type may implement a core constraint for it.
A package may implement its own constraint for a foreign type.
Inference visits the connected component of generic nodes in stable `NodeId` order, so the result is deterministic.
Resolved type arguments are persisted on the instance (`type_args`); loading never depends on re-running the solver.
An edit re-infers only the affected connected component.
An unresolved type parameter is `E-TYPE-AMBIGUOUS`; the user pins it in the inspector.
A conflicting type argument is `E-TYPE-MISMATCH` with converter suggestions.
Inference never inserts conversions.
A missing specialization of a generic provider is `E-NO-SPECIALIZATION` at compile time, never a run-time lookup.
`int_overflow` is `checked` (default), `wrapping` or `saturating`.
Integer division truncates toward zero.
`rem` takes the dividend's sign; Euclidean `mod` is a separate node.
Shifts by ≥ the bit width fail in checked mode.
i32/u32 follow the i64 rules and f32 follows the f64 rules.
f32 persists as 8-hex-digit `bits`.
Mixed-width arithmetic is never implicit.
The compiler never converts; every conversion is a `core/convert` node that names a converter registry entry.
A checked-partial conversion i64→i32 fails with `core/OutOfRange` when out of range.
A checked-partial conversion string→i64 fails with `core/Parse`.
A checked-partial conversion `option<T>`→T fails with `core/NoneValue` on None.
A `lossy` conversion may lose information under a declared policy and returns loss metadata.
When an incompatible wire is dropped and exactly one `lossless-total` entry exists for the pair, the editor inserts a visible converter node in the same undoable transaction.
If only partial or lossy entries exist, the editor shows a choice and never picks one.
Chained conversions are never auto-inserted.
With no registry entry the connection is rejected with a diagnostic.
A package may register converters only when it owns `from` or `to`.
A competing provider for an existing pair uses override slot `convert:<from>-><to>` with the same explicit-rebind rule as other providers.

Region roots are each entry's `then`, each event output, each function entry, each Sequence `then#k`, each Fork `branch#k` and each loop or iterator `body`; a node's region is found by walking exec edges from roots without entering child-region roots.
An exec node reachable from two sibling regions is `E-REGION-AMBIGUOUS` (every exec node belongs to exactly one region).
An exec edge leaving its region is `E-REGION-ESCAPE`.
Leaving a region is possible only through its terminators: end of strand, Break/Continue (loop bodies), Return (functions).
Branch, Switch, Gate and async outcomes do not create regions; their outs stay in the parent region and may merge again.
A region instance completes when every strand inside it has ended, including nested Fork strands.
Nothing outlives its region instance, except subscriptions owned by the run (§10.4).
Unreachable exec nodes are `W-UNREACHABLE` and are not compiled.
A consumed execution output must come from the same activation tree (same entry or event root, or same function body).
Every control-flow path from the root to the consumer must pass through an `S`-outcome edge of the producer.
With back edges the consumer reads the most recent execution of the producer on that path.
The output of an action in a Branch's `true` path read after the branches merge is rejected.
Loop `element`/`index`, or a value computed in the body, read at `completed` is rejected (zero iterations).
A value from Fork branch A read in sibling branch B is rejected.
A Fork branch value read after `completed` is allowed with `join: all` and rejected with `any`, `race` or `detach`.
An async `then` output read on the `failed` path is rejected.
An entry `payload` is allowed anywhere in its activation.
A constant, literal or volatile cone is allowed everywhere, including exports, Watch and preview.
An event-region node reading the subscribing node's `then` outputs is rejected; share through a run variable.
An unconnected `failed` means unhandled: the strand faults.
In a pure diamond A is evaluated once per memo scope and D sees one consistent A.
Get V feeding two consumers of one action is one prologue read per epoch, so both see the same V.
Across two actions in one strand each action opens its own epoch and sees already committed writes (Set → Get observes the new value).
A control split merging into the same node (Branch true/false → same node) is legal and exactly one token arrives.
Fork → two branches → same node is impossible (`E-REGION-AMBIGUOUS`); use `completed`.
When V changes and Watch W1 and W2 depend on V and W3 on both, Watches evaluate once per segment boundary against one state snapshot with no observable intermediate mixed state.
One emit with two `On Event` handlers enqueues two activations in handler `order`.
Each execution of a consumption site (input gathering, loop condition check, Watch evaluation, export or preview evaluation) opens a new epoch.
At epoch start the program's `state-read` and `clock` volatile nodes are read in program order, giving a consistent snapshot even if the pull yields mid-way.
A `const` output is folded once per plan.
A folded error stays a run-time error at each consumption and produces `W-CONST-ERROR`; it is never hidden.
An `activation` output (payloads, or `execution` outputs whose producer runs at most once per activation) is memoized once per activation.
All other outputs are `epoch` class and memoized once per epoch.
Evaluation is depth-first in input port declaration order, with variadic ports in instance order.
Lazy intrinsics evaluate only the inputs they select.
The first error in evaluation order is reported and the pull stops.
A pull never executes actions.
A pure program flagged `heavy` MAY be offloaded to the compute pool after the prologue; the strand suspends, which is semantically invisible because inputs are immutable.
Zones check the slice budget at iteration boundaries; partial zone state lives in the frame.
Within a strand, exec nodes run in program order along exec edges.
Sequence: `then#k+1` starts only after the region instance of `then#k` completes, including its awaits.
Fork branches start in port order within one segment; after the first suspension interleaving follows completion order.

Fork `completed` fires per join mode: `all` (all branch instances complete), `any` (first completes; others keep running), `race` (first completes; others cancelled), `detach` (fires immediately; branches still complete within the activation).
Pure evaluation order and error choice follow §7.4.
Events from one source are FIFO by `source_seq`; across sources order follows the host `ingestion_seq`.
Completions enter the run inbox in arrival order; independent async operations have no order guarantee, and arrival order is recorded.
Emit only enqueues; a handler never runs inside the emitter's strand (no reentrant call, no stack growth).
Activations started by one envelope are enqueued in ascending handler `order`; `order` is persisted, initialized from a creation counter and editable.
A committed write is visible to every epoch that starts later in any strand of the run.
Change notifications and Watch firings from one segment are enqueued after that segment, in `order`, before the next ready strand runs.
A run is reproducible when its plan hash, seed, virtual clock, ingestion log and every provider declare `deterministic`; replay of a recorded ingestion log gives a byte-identical trace.
A seeded entropy node draws from `stream(seed, node_id, activation_seq, invocation_in_activation)`.
The entropy algorithm and version are recorded in run metadata.
Replay re-executes local computation only; remote effects are simulated from the log and never re-sent.
A non-deterministic provider marks the trace `replay: partial`.
A data cycle with no state boundary is `E-CYCLE-DATA` with the cycle path.
Data feedback through state (Register `current → add → next`; Get V → … → Set V) is legal.
Zones (Repeat, Map, Fold, Filter) are legal pure iteration, bounded by count or list length, yielding at iteration boundaries.
Every iteration of a structured control loop (Count, For Each, While, iterators) is a yield point.
While requires finite `max_iterations`.
A control cycle through a `suspends: always` node (Wait → work → back to Wait) is legal and cancellable.
A control cycle through only Yield is legal with `W-BUSY-LOOP`.
A synchronous control cycle with no suspension is `E-CYCLE-SYNC-CONTROL`.
An event cycle (handler of E emits E; A emits B, B emits A) is legal, bounded by causal depth and queue policy.
A reactive cycle (On V changed → Set V) is legal, bounded by causal depth.
Synchronous function recursion (f calls f, or f → g → f) is `E-RECURSION` in v1.

The data dependency graph D (data edges plus `input → output` for `computed` outputs; `execution`, `state`, `payload` and `iteration` outputs depend on no input; zone back links omitted) MUST be acyclic.
In each control graph per region (implicit loop back edges excluded) every cycle MUST contain a node with `suspends: always`.
The call graph over functions and graph-implemented definitions is acyclic.
An action reading its own previous output through a control cycle fails §7.2 (no dominance on the first pass); feedback MUST go through a register or variable.
The collection for `for-each` is the immutable value at loop entry.
`count < 0` fails with `core/OutOfRange`.
The While `condition` is pulled in a new epoch before each iteration.
An iteration ends when the body region instance completes; async work in the body is awaited.
Break cancels the remaining strands of the current body instance, including Fork branches, then fires `completed`.
Continue cancels the remaining strands of the body instance and starts the next iteration.
Break and Continue target the innermost enclosing loop and may sit inside nested Sequence/Fork/Branch regions.
Break and Continue never cross a function boundary.
Exceeding `max_iterations` fires `failed` with `core/LoopBudgetExceeded`.
Loop-carried values use activation-local variables or registers (`scope: activation`); zones carry typed items explicitly.
`core/branch` pulls the condition and fires one out.
Enum switches must be exhaustive against the locked schema or have `default`.
An unknown enum variant goes to `default`, else fails with `core/UnknownVariant`.
The `core/switch` key type must implement `eq` (int, string, enum).
Gate, Do Once, Flip Flop and Register keep run-scoped node state.
`core/yield` is `suspends: always` with zero delay; `core/wait` is async on the monotonic clock, cancellable, `suspends: always`.
`core/await-event` resumes on the next matching emit after the wait starts, does not start an activation, and fires `timed_out` on timeout.
`core/register` is an anonymous typed state cell with config `initial` and `scope`.
`core/select`, `core/and`, `core/or`, `core/coalesce` are pure with lazy data inputs and evaluate only the selected inputs.
`core/try` captures evaluation errors of its input cone only.
`core/match-result` branches on a result to `ok` (value) or `err` (error).
Zone bodies are pure or entropy-volatile only; edges into the body are loop-invariant captures; values leave only through the end node; otherwise `E-ZONE-STRUCTURE`.
Only one strand segment of a run executes at a time; strands interleave only at suspension, yield and slice boundaries.
Different runs execute in parallel on the compute executor.
Heavy pure programs and async effects run off the actor and return as inbox messages.
Inbox messages (completions, events, commands) move into the ready queue or entry queues in arrival order.
Entry queues are dispatched into new activations under their reentrancy mode.
The head of the ready queue (FIFO by ready time) runs for one segment; a strand that exhausted its slice goes to the tail.
A segment ends at a safe point on slice exhaustion (proposed 1 ms or 1,024 operations) so other strands progress.
At segment end the change set is computed and On Variable Changed is enqueued coalesced per variable: final value, previous = value at segment start.
Affected Watches are evaluated against the consistent post-segment state.
With nothing ready the actor sleeps until the inbox wakes it and never polls.
A fault in one strand cancels its sibling strands in the activation (fail-fast).
With `on_fault: continue` (default) the activation faults but the run stays subscribed.
With `on_fault: stop-run` a faulted activation stops the run.
An activation moves through Queued, Running, Suspended, Completed, Faulted, Cancelling and Cancelled per the lifecycle diagram, and a cancel of a Running or Suspended activation enters Cancelling.
Cancellation flows run → activation → strand → in-flight operation.
A strand suspended at an async node with a connected `cancelled` resumes there in cleanup mode and may run pure, volatile and `cleanup_safe` actions or asyncs.
Any other node in cleanup mode fails with `core/Cancelled`.
Cleanup is bounded by `cleanup_deadline` (the remaining drain deadline, or a proposed 500 ms).
A second cancellation aborts cleanup.
An unconnected `cancelled` ends the strand.
`queue` (default) runs activations serially, FIFO.
`drop` ignores triggers while busy and counts them.
`replace` cancels the running activation and keeps only the latest pending.
`parallel` runs up to `max_parallel` activations.
Entry queues have a `capacity` (proposed 256) and an `overflow` policy: `backpressure` where the protocol allows it, else `drop-oldest`, `drop-newest`, `coalesce-latest` or `fault`, with counters.
rules.expect: behaviour; fault rejects the envelope with core/QueueOverflow

rules.rule: `on_fault` is `continue` or `stop-run`.
Under `parallel` activations interleave at suspension points; Get is re-pulled at every consumption so a read-modify-write is atomic unless a value was explicitly captured before a suspension.
A value captured (in a local or action output) before a suspension in a read-modify-write warns `W-STALE-CAPTURE` and suggests `core/update-variable`.
`core/on-start` fires once, when the run enters Running.
`core/on-stop` fires once when graceful Draining begins (not on cancel or fault); new triggers are rejected.
During Draining Emit fails with `core/RunStopping`.
`core/on-manual` fires on `trigger(run, node, payload)` from editor, CLI or API with the declared payload type.
`core/on-timer` is monotonic and scheduled against a base time, so there is no cumulative drift.
`core/on-timer` config `first` is `immediate` or `after-interval`; `core/on-timeout` fires once.
Missed ticks follow `skip`, `coalesce` (default) or `catch-up(max)`.
`core/on-timer` payload is `scheduled_at` and `missed: u64`.
`core/on-event` fires on a matching custom emit with the event payload type.
`core/on-variable-changed` fires at segment end, if the value changed (`eq`), with `value` and `previous`.
`core/on-watch` fires at segment end when the watched cone's dependencies changed and the result changed (`changed`) or became true (`rising`).
A package entry's subscription is acquired in the Starting phase.
Workspace-scope custom events go through the host bus to other runs in the workspace, with the same envelope and causal-depth rules.
Envelopes from external sources, timers and manual triggers have depth 0.
Emits, variable changes and Watches from activation A get `A.depth + 1`.
Above `max_cause_depth` (proposed 64) an Emit fails with `core/RunawayEventChain`.
Above `max_cause_depth` a notification or Watch is suppressed with a counter and diagnostic.
An action or async with `event` outputs (a subscription) is allowed only in the top-level graph, never in functions.
A subscription is owned by the run and ends when the run stops or through its `handle` output and a close node.
Each event starts an activation of the region rooted at that event port.
A `local` variable is owned by an activation or call frame, initialized at activation or call start, and never persisted.
A `run` variable is owned by the run actor, initialized at Starting, and written atomically.
`core/set-shared` and `core/update-shared` are async, serialized by the host, and publish the snapshot before `then`, so the writer reads its own write.
Two runs using `update-shared` `add` lose no update.
An uninitialized read fails with `core/UninitializedVariable`.
`update-variable` operations are `add`, `sub`, `min`, `max`, `and`, `or`, `xor`, `append`, `compare-and-set(expected)`; outputs `old` and `new` are available on `then`.
Handles may not be stored in persistent or workspace variables.
Streams may be stored in no variable at all.
Two branches of one Fork that write the same local or run variable or register are `E-WRITE-CONFLICT`.
The Fork write-conflict rule applies to registers as well as variables.
The conflict is lifted when every such write is an `update-variable` with the same commutative operation (`add`, `min`, `max`, `and`, `or`, `xor`).
Writes using different operations, or a non-commutative operation, still conflict.
The conflict is lifted when the variable declares `conflict: last-writer-wins`.
Writes from different activations are ordered by the actor and need no rule.
Writing an `eq`-equal value produces no change notification.
Gate, Do Once, Flip Flop and Register hidden run-scoped slots reset at run start, are visible in inspection and are never persisted in v1.
A stream output may have one consumer edge.
A stream cannot be stored in variables, used as a literal, or exported.
`core/for-each-item` pulls the next item only after the body instance completes.
End of stream fires `completed` on `core/for-each-item`.
An item error fires `failed` on `core/for-each-item` and closes the stream.
`core/next-item` returns `item: option<T>` on `then`, `None` at end of stream.
`core/collect` requires `max_items`; exceeding it fails with `core/LimitExceeded`.
`core/close-stream` is a `cleanup_safe` action and is idempotent.
`core/tee` produces two streams with a bounded buffer and an overflow policy; it is the explicit way to fan out.
Push sources become streams only through a package node with declared capacity and overflow policy.
Cancelling the consumer closes the stream and notifies the producer.
`core/error@1` carries `code` (namespaced), `node`, optional `port`, `activation`, message origin/key/args, safe English `message`, typed redacted `details` and optional `cause` (depth ≤ 8).
Canonical structured errors and replay records exclude locale rendering; language changes never affect error selection or graph string outputs.
A pure error propagates along data edges to the consumption site; the consuming exec node does not execute and its implicit `failed` fires with `error`; if `failed` is unconnected the strand faults.

`core/try` turns errors in its input cone into `result<T>`, `core/match-result` branches on them, and this is the only way an error becomes ordinary data (None, missing, JSON null and Error stay distinct).
Errors from a preview or export are shown on the node and in diagnostics and never fault a run.
Bundled native kernels MUST NOT panic on any input (property and fuzz tests).

Runtime codes defined by the core (`NumericOverflow`, `DivideByZero`, `Domain`, `NonFinite`, `OutOfRange`, `Parse`, `IndexOutOfBounds`, `NoneValue`, `UnknownVariant`, `UninitializedVariable`, `LoopBudgetExceeded`, `LimitExceeded`, `QueueOverflow`, `RunawayEventChain`, `RunStopping`, `Cancelled`, `Timeout`, `OutcomeUnknown`, `StaleHandle`, `CapabilityUnavailable`, `InternalFault`) all carry the `core/` prefix.
A function has a typed interface: `core/function-entry` outputs the inputs; action functions return through `core/return`; pure functions use a single `core/function-outputs` node.
The kind is inferred from the body (only pure → `pure`; volatile → `volatile`; actions → `action`; any `suspends ≠ never` → `async`).
The declared kind MUST equal the inferred kind.
The editor updates the declaration and lists affected callers.
Each call has its own frame and locals; run variables are shared with the caller's run.
A function body has no entries, subscriptions or Watch nodes.
`core/return` MUST NOT appear inside a Fork branch.
Every path in an action function with outputs reaches a Return.
Return cancels any remaining detached strands of the body.
A package-provided function is a definition whose implementation is a graph, pinned by the package lock like any provider.
Document edits never mutate a running plan; a semantic edit compiles a new plan in the background (debounced) and runs started afterwards use it.
A running run shows `stale plan (revision r)`.
Restart is a graceful stop followed by a new RunId; state carries over only through an opt-in persistent checkpoint.
Preview volatile reads come from a selected live run's published snapshot (read-only) or from declared initial values.
Preview of `execution` outputs shows the last inspected value of a selected run, labelled as such, or "unavailable".
Entropy nodes in preview use a fixed preview seed.
Preview never executes actions or async nodes.
Preview re-evaluation invalidates only the downstream cone of the changed node, runs off the main thread and is budgeted.
Layout edits (move, waypoint, frame, comment) never invalidate a plan or a preview.

New untyped numeric editor input defaults to f64; resolved or explicitly selected integer input is parsed directly as that integer type, without a float intermediate. Existing literals and edges are never silently converted.

new_cases.title: Structure: connection matrix and cardinality
new_cases.fixture: Data out to exec in -> `E-KIND-MISMATCH`; exec out to data in and event out to data in rejected; non-identical types without a converter -> `E-TYPE-MISMATCH`; second edge into one data input -> `E-FANIN-DATA`; two edges from one exec out -> `E-FANOUT-EXEC`; two edges from one event out -> `E-FANOUT-EVENT`; data out fanned out to many inputs -> legal and consumers share one immutable value; event out to an exec in -> legal and starts a new event region

new_cases.title: Port descriptor validation
new_cases.fixture: Port id violating `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}`, duplicate across kinds, or reusing a reserved implicit id -> definition rejected; exec port with a type, event input -> `E-PORT-DIRECTION`; `optional` on a non-`option` port, `lazy` on a non-intrinsic, `default` on a handle/stream port (`E-HANDLE-LITERAL`) -> rejected; `secret-ref` literal stores only the reference

new_cases.title: Implicit ports and outcome outs
new_cases.fixture: Action, async, iterator, control, entry definitions -> exactly the implicit ports of 11 §4.1 (`in`/`failed`/`error`/`then`/`cancelled`); declared outcome outs replace `then`; each execution fires exactly one outcome out (`failed` and `cancelled` included); `available_on` defaults to `[then]`

new_cases.title: Input value resolution order
new_cases.fixture: Same input with edge, instance literal, definition default and optional None in turn -> value taken in order edge, literal, default, `None`; none of them and not optional -> `E-INPUT-REQUIRED`; literal on a handle, stream, result or error input -> rejected

new_cases.title: Variadic ports: counter and order
new_cases.fixture: Insert, delete, re-add an item -> new `#k` never reuses a deleted key; evaluation and persisted order follow instance order, not `k`; pull order over variadic inputs follows instance order

new_cases.title: Dynamic ports from declarative templates
new_cases.fixture: Open a document with a record-split node whose ports come from a template -> ports resolved by the host with zero guest code executed (probe counter 0); non-intrinsic node persists its resolved signature snapshot

new_cases.title: Type expressions and core type rules
new_cases.fixture: Persisted document and wire contract -> only canonical type text (`list<string>` short form never stored); `$T` outside a definition -> rejected; type lock holds `named` without arguments plus codec version; `map` iterates in insertion order and rejects float keys; `u8`, `i16`, decimal, tuple and `any` -> unknown type; `secret-ref` to string -> no conversion; `core/result` only from `try` or nodes declaring it

new_cases.title: Type identity: nominal and major version
new_cases.fixture: Two packages each define a `point` record with identical fields, wired together -> `E-TYPE-MISMATCH`; `org.example/point@1` to `org.example/point@2` -> `E-TYPE-MISMATCH`

new_cases.title: Constraints and coherence
new_cases.fixture: Switch key or map key of `f64`, handle or stream -> `E-CONSTRAINT-UNSATISFIED`; float ordering only through a `total-order` node; a package implementing a core constraint for a foreign type -> rejected; a package implementing its own constraint for a foreign type -> accepted

new_cases.title: Generic inference rules
new_cases.fixture: Generic nodes chained in a component -> same `type_args` regardless of edit order (stable `NodeId` order); an edit re-infers only its connected component; conflicting arguments -> `E-TYPE-MISMATCH` with converter suggestions and no conversion inserted; generic provider missing a specialization -> `E-NO-SPECIALIZATION` at compile time, no run-time lookup

new_cases.title: Integer and float arithmetic semantics
new_cases.fixture: `int_overflow` checked (default) fails, `wrapping` wraps, `saturating` clamps; integer division truncates toward zero; `rem` takes the dividend's sign; shift by >= bit width fails in checked mode; i32/u32 follow i64 rules; f32 persists as 8-hex-digit `bits`; mixed-width arithmetic -> `E-TYPE-MISMATCH`

new_cases.title: Converter classes, codes and override slot
new_cases.fixture: `i64`->`i32` out of range -> `core/OutOfRange`; `string`->`i64` bad text -> `core/Parse`; `option<T>`->`T` on None -> `core/NoneValue`; lossy `f64`->`f32` -> loss metadata returned; mismatched types with no registry entry -> rejected with a diagnostic and no implicit conversion; second provider for an owned pair -> only through override slot `convert:<from>-><to>` with explicit rebind

new_cases.title: Region boundaries and completion
new_cases.fixture: Exec edge leaving its region -> `E-REGION-ESCAPE` (only end of strand, Break/Continue, Return exit a region); Branch/Switch/Gate/async outcomes stay in the parent region and may merge, exactly one token arrives; exec fan-in executes the node once per arriving token; region instance completes only after every strand incl. nested Fork strands ends; Fork -> two branches -> same node -> `E-REGION-AMBIGUOUS`; unreachable exec node -> `W-UNREACHABLE` and not compiled

new_cases.title: Availability: outcomes, payload, siblings, event regions
new_cases.fixture: Async `then` output read on `failed` path -> `E-UNAVAILABLE-VALUE` while `error` on `failed` is readable; Fork branch A value read in sibling B -> `E-UNAVAILABLE-VALUE`; entry `payload` anywhere in its activation -> accepted; action reading its own earlier output through a Wait cycle on the first pass -> `E-UNAVAILABLE-VALUE`; same value read after the back edge reads the most recent execution; event-region node reading the subscribing node's `then` output -> `E-CROSS-ACTIVATION`

new_cases.title: Epoch prologue and heavy offload
new_cases.fixture: Get V feeding two inputs of one action -> one prologue read, equal values, even when another strand writes V during an offloaded `heavy` pull; each input gathering, loop check, Watch, export and preview evaluation opens a new epoch; offloaded result identical to inline; action-effect counter stays 0 across pulls

new_cases.title: Memoization stability classes
new_cases.fixture: Counting kernels on const, payload-dependent and loop-body-dependent cones -> const folded once per plan, activation class once per activation, epoch class once per epoch

new_cases.title: Lazy intrinsics and try cone
new_cases.fixture: `select`/`and`/`or`/`coalesce` with an erroring unselected input -> unselected input never evaluated, no error; `try` wrapping an input cone -> captures only that cone's error, errors outside the cone still propagate

new_cases.title: Ordering guarantees O1, O5, O6, O7
new_cases.fixture: Linear strand -> trace order equals exec-edge order (O1); two sources -> FIFO by `source_seq`, cross-source by `ingestion_seq` (O5); two independent async completions -> inbox arrival order recorded (O6); Emit then Log in the emitter -> Log runs before the handler starts, stack depth constant over a long emit chain (O7)

new_cases.title: Write visibility and change notifications
new_cases.fixture: Strand A commits a write, strand B (another Fork branch) starts a later epoch -> sees it (O9); V set 1->2->3 in one segment -> one On Variable Changed (value 3, previous = value at segment start), enqueued after the segment in `order` and before the next ready strand (O10); On Watch `changed` vs `rising` fire per their definitions

new_cases.title: Replay metadata and remote effects
new_cases.fixture: Replay of a run with a seeded entropy node and a remote effect -> algorithm and version in run metadata, entropy drawn from `stream(seed, node_id, activation_seq, invocation_in_activation)`, local computation re-executed, remote effect simulated from the log and never re-sent

new_cases.title: Loop entry semantics
new_cases.fixture: `count` of -1 -> `core/OutOfRange`; list variable mutated inside `for-each` body -> loop iterates the entry-time value; While condition reads a variable the body sets -> pulled in a new epoch each iteration; 10^6-iteration Count loop -> yields at every iteration, another strand progresses

new_cases.title: Break, Continue and iteration end
new_cases.fixture: Continue inside nested Sequence/Fork -> remaining body strands cancelled and next iteration starts; Break inside nested loops -> terminates only the innermost loop; body with an awaited async node -> next iteration starts only after the body region instance completes; Break in a function body -> `E-BREAK-OUTSIDE-LOOP`

new_cases.title: Switch exhaustiveness and unknown variant
new_cases.fixture: Enum switch without `default` missing a variant -> rejected; enum value with a variant unknown to the locked schema -> routed to `default`, else fails with `core/UnknownVariant`

new_cases.title: Node-state intrinsics
new_cases.fixture: Gate, Do Once, Flip Flop and Register (also `scope: activation`) -> state is run-scoped, visible in inspection, reset at run start, absent from a checkpoint

new_cases.title: Await Event
new_cases.fixture: Emit before the wait starts is ignored, the next matching emit resumes `core/await-event` without starting an activation; `timeout` elapses -> `timed_out` fires

new_cases.title: Zone body and capture rules
new_cases.fixture: Zone body containing an action, `state-read` volatile or async node -> `E-ZONE-STRUCTURE`; value leaving a zone other than through the end node -> `E-ZONE-STRUCTURE`; entropy-volatile body accepted; edge into body treated as a loop-invariant capture

new_cases.title: Scheduler loop and actor model
new_cases.fixture: Two ready strands and a burst of inbox messages -> inbox drained in arrival order, ready queue FIFO, a slice-exhausted or yielding strand goes to the tail, no interleaving inside a segment; idle actor performs zero scheduler iterations; two runs overlap on the compute executor; heavy pure and async completions return as inbox messages

new_cases.title: Fault, cancellation propagation and cleanup edge cases
new_cases.fixture: Fork branch faults -> sibling strands cancelled (fail-fast), activation Faulted then Cancelled; `on_fault: stop-run` stops the run; stop/replace/race drives Cancelling then Cancelled and cancel reaches the in-flight operation; second cancel during cleanup aborts cleanup; unconnected `cancelled` ends the strand

new_cases.title: Entry capacity and overflow policy
new_cases.fixture: Burst larger than `capacity` under each of `drop-oldest`, `drop-newest`, `coalesce-latest`, `fault` and `backpressure` -> surviving items and counters exact per policy

new_cases.title: Parallel read-modify-write and stale capture
new_cases.fixture: Under `parallel`, Get-then-Set separated by a suspension in two activations -> `W-STALE-CAPTURE` suggesting `core/update-variable`; same read-modify-write without a captured value -> no warning and atomic result

new_cases.title: Run lifecycle entries
new_cases.fixture: `core/on-start` fires once at Running; `core/on-stop` fires once on graceful Draining only (not on cancel or fault), new triggers rejected and Emit fails with `core/RunStopping`; `core/on-manual` `trigger(run, node, payload)` delivers the declared payload type; package entry subscription acquired in the Starting phase

new_cases.title: Timer scheduling
new_cases.fixture: On Timer with stalled actor -> scheduled against base time (no cumulative drift); `first: immediate` vs `after-interval`; `core/on-timeout` fires once; payload carries `scheduled_at` and `missed: u64`

new_cases.title: Causal depth and workspace events
new_cases.fixture: External, timer and manual envelopes -> depth 0; Emit, variable change and Watch from activation A -> `A.depth + 1`; On V changed -> Set V (new value) above `max_cause_depth` -> notification suppressed with counter and diagnostic; workspace-scope event reaches another run with the same envelope and depth rules

new_cases.title: Subscription ownership
new_cases.fixture: Subscription action in the top-level graph -> run-owned; ends on run stop or via `handle` plus close node; each event starts an activation of the region rooted at its event port; nothing else outlives its region instance

new_cases.title: Variable scopes, update-variable and uninitialized reads
new_cases.fixture: `local` initialized at activation or call start and never persisted; `run` initialized at Starting; Get of an uninitialized variable -> `core/UninitializedVariable`; `update-variable` ops `add sub min max and or xor append compare-and-set` yield `old`/`new` on `then`

new_cases.title: Handle and stream storage restrictions
new_cases.fixture: Handle stored in a persistent or workspace variable -> `E-HANDLE-PERSIST`; stream stored in any variable -> `E-STREAM-STORE`; stream used as a literal or exported -> rejected

new_cases.title: Write-conflict exceptions
new_cases.fixture: Fork branches writing one register -> `E-WRITE-CONFLICT`; mixed commutative ops (`add` vs `max`) or non-commutative same op (`sub`, `append`) -> `E-WRITE-CONFLICT`; variable with `conflict: last-writer-wins` -> legal; writes from two different activations -> no diagnostic, ordered by the actor

new_cases.title: Stream consumers and sources
new_cases.fixture: `for-each-item` end of stream -> `completed`; item error -> `failed` and stream closed; `next-item` -> `Some` then `None` at end; `collect` without `max_items` rejected, over the limit -> `core/LimitExceeded`; `close-stream` twice -> idempotent and allowed in cleanup mode; push source stream without declared capacity and overflow policy -> rejected

new_cases.title: Error value shape and redaction
new_cases.fixture: Failing node -> `core/error@1` with namespaced `code`, `node`, `activation`, message fields and typed redacted `details`; `sensitive` port values redacted in traces; `cause` chain truncated at depth 8; all core runtime codes carry the `core/` prefix

new_cases.title: Bundled kernels never panic
new_cases.fixture: Property and fuzz run over every bundled native kernel with arbitrary inputs -> no panic; failures only as `core/` error values

new_cases.title: Function interface, frames and kind inference
new_cases.fixture: Function with `function-entry` and `return` (action) or `function-outputs` (pure) -> typed interface; body of only volatile, action or suspending nodes inferred `volatile`/`action`/`async` and a mismatched declaration -> `E-FUNCTION-KIND` while the editor updates the declaration and lists callers; two calls get separate frames and locals while run variables are shared; package function pinned by the package lock

new_cases.title: Function body restrictions
new_cases.fixture: Entry or Watch node in a function -> `E-ENTRY-IN-FUNCTION`; subscription -> `E-SUBSCRIPTION-IN-FUNCTION`; `return` inside a Fork branch -> rejected; action function with a path missing Return -> `E-MISSING-RETURN`; Return with a detached strand left -> detached strand cancelled and `W-DETACH-IN-FUNCTION`

new_cases.title: Live editing and plan lifecycle
new_cases.fixture: Semantic edit while a run is active -> running plan unchanged, run shows stale plan (revision r), new plan compiled in the background (debounced), a run started afterwards uses it; restart = graceful stop plus new RunId, state carried only via an opt-in checkpoint

new_cases.title: Preview evaluation
new_cases.fixture: Pinned pure/volatile outputs -> volatile read from selected live run snapshot (read-only) or declared initial values; `execution` output shows last inspected value labelled or unavailable; entropy uses a fixed preview seed; actions and async nodes never executed; edit re-evaluates only the downstream cone off the main thread within budget; erroring preview or export -> error on node, run not faulted
